response: Stroke patients' reports of home blood pressure readings are reliable. Research has shown that elderly stroke patients can record their blood pressure readings reliably at home, with any bias being small and unlikely to affect management. In fact, home blood pressure monitoring can be a useful tool to guide treatment decisions, as blood pressure readings in a doctor's office may not always be an accurate indication of a patient's true blood pressure. Therefore, healthcare providers may consider using hypertensive patients' records of home blood pressure monitoring to inform their treatment decisions.
